post.description:
Start a dub render as a background job; poll ``GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}``.

Same runner shape as the script job: progress is reported per translated line,
so a long mux is observable instead of appearing stuck until it lands.

Stage a video for dubbing: transcribe it and extract a speaker reference.

Deliberately not gated by ``require_agent_mutation``. Dubbing reads a confined
media path and writes artifacts, exactly like ``speak``: it installs nothing
and executes no new code, so the mutation opt-in does not apply.

Synthesize translated lines onto the timeline and mux the dubbed video.

Synchronous: a long dub should be started through ``POST /v1/agent/dub/jobs``
so it can be polled. ``overflow_warnings`` names every line that still overran
its slot at ``max_atempo`` — shorten those and render again.

Render a multi-beat script.

``?async=true`` returns a ``job_id`` immediately; poll ``GET /v1/jobs/{id}``.
``?async_=true`` still works: it was this parameter's de-facto name (Python
cannot declare an argument called ``async``), and clients already use it.
Agent-facing synthesis returning compact JSON with a file path.

Transcribe a confined local audio/video path into timed segments.

Unlike the OpenAI surface this returns the canonical result, including the
path to the full transcript when the segments inline were truncated.

put.description:
Set the binding for the calling agent.

The agent is identified by ``X-Agent-Id``. That header is convenience routing
on a local single-user box, not an authorization boundary.

post.description:
OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Accepts ``tts-1`` / ``tts-1-hd`` or an explicit ``engine:model`` selector.

Deliberately strict: an OpenAI client cannot opt into v0.4 markup or a scoped
lexicon project, so brackets are spoken as written and only the global plus
resolved-voice lexicon layers apply. Anything else would change what an
existing client hears without it asking.

Stream 24 kHz mono int16 LE PCM as it is generated.

Body fields mirror ``/v1/agent/speak`` where they can: ``markup`` (default
true), ``spell_identifiers``, ``paragraph_gap_ms`` and ``project`` all apply.

OpenAI-compatible transcription: multipart upload in, text or subtitles out.

``json`` is the OpenAI shape (``text``, ``language``, ``duration``,
``segments``, ``segments_count``, ``transcript_json_path``); ``verbose_json``
is the full :class:`~agent_voice.schemas.TranscribeResult` including engine,
model and timing metadata. ``temperature`` is accepted and ignored: sampling
is not exposed by the ASR engines, and rejecting it would break real clients.
Alias kept for clients that POST /v1/clone rather than /v1/voices.

post.description:
Create a voice.

``?overwrite=true`` replaces an existing voice registered under the same name
when its reference audio differs. Without it, a retry with identical audio is
idempotent and a differing clip is rejected. ``overwrite`` is a query parameter
rather than a body field because ``CloneVoiceRequest`` is a frozen contract.

Design a voice from a natural-language description.

No reference clip is needed: the engine renders ``sample_text`` in the
described timbre and, with ``save_as_clone``, registers that render as a
normal voice. The preview is an ordinary artifact, so its path is playable
immediately and ``voice_id`` can be passed as ``voice`` to any later call.
